summary: Natural, slightly more literary Dutch than V2 (toen-clause first in b076, 'terwijl' in b080, particles 'toch', 'wel') but fully inside the profile: no restricted construction, no sentence over 20 words. The vocabulary FAIL is entirely tool-driven ('wél' is accented 'wel', 'haarne' is a bad lemma, 'drugsgeld' a transparent compound); real new lemmas are the 2 stretch words. Secondary: the simile 'als uit het vuur' and a gloss on the known word 'schor'.

findings.fragment: trok zijn hand omlaag als uit het vuur
findings.problem: 'als uit het vuur' is not a Dutch idiom; the compressed simile reads as a translation and makes the reader re-parse (as if the hand came out of a fire).
findings.evidence: No Dutch collocation 'als uit het vuur'; the natural form needs 'alsof' (R-CONJ-OTHER), so the comparison must be made explicit instead.
findings.required_fix: Make the comparison explicit with an allowed frame: 'Harry trok zijn hand omlaag, zo snel als uit een vuur, en verstopte de envelop achter zijn rug als drugsgeld.' Optionally detach the second simile as a fragment: '… achter zijn rug. Als drugsgeld.'

findings.problem: Two glosses in a 12-word paragraph on words the lexicon already marks as known.
findings.evidence: lexicon: schor = known A2 (c3529), gefluister = known A2 (c4473); gloss_per_paragraph_max 2 reached on known words.
findings.required_fix: Drop the gloss on 'schor' (write 'een schor \gl{gefluister}{whisper}'); the gloss on gefluister may stay only because exceptions.json asks to gloss fluisteren at first occurrence.

findings.problem: Tool reports 'wél' as unknown; it is 'wel' (A1) with the standard Dutch stress accent.
findings.evidence: lexicon: wel known A1 (c648); accent not normalised by the tool.
findings.required_fix: No change. (Accent plus \emph is double emphasis; either alone would do, but both are correct Dutch.)

findings.problem: Tool rates it hard (nt2lex C1); for the reader it is a transparent compound of two A1 words and the bible fixes the rendering.
findings.evidence: lexicon: drug = known A1, geld = known A1; bible.md ch 1 traps: 'drug money' → drugsgeld; 'replace-or-gloss' action dismissed.
findings.required_fix: No change; leave unglossed. Lexicon owner: add 'drugsgeld' as known compound.

findings.problem: Tool lemma 'haarne' is a mis-lemmatised diminutive; the word is haar + net + -je, all known.
findings.evidence: lexicon: haar known, net (NOUN) known A1; vocabulary row 'haarne' status unknown dismissed.

findings.problem: Unknown lemma, but it carries the scene (embarrassment comedy) and has no plain equivalent with the same meaning for this reader.
findings.evidence: lexicon: gênant absent; 'pijnlijk' (B1) was learned as 'painful', 'stom' shifts the meaning; already glossed.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is. Lexicon owner: consider adding gênant (very frequent spoken word).

findings.problem: Unknown lemma; the plain alternative 'hek' (A2) is an open fence, and the image needs a solid one she must peer over.
findings.evidence: lexicon: schutting absent, hek known A2 'fence'; already glossed; block at the 2-gloss limit.
findings.required_fix: Keep as is; switch to 'het hek van de buren' only if the gloss budget of b086 is needed elsewhere.

findings.problem: 'behoorlijk' is known to this reader as an adjective ('proper, fitting'); the degree-adverb sense ('pretty, quite') is a different sense that the card does not cover.
findings.evidence: lexicon: behoorlijk known A2, en = reasonable/fitting/proper; V1/V2 use 'best', which the reader knows in exactly this sense.
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'eigenlijk best gênant'. Context makes 'behoorlijk' guessable, so no round is needed for this alone.

findings.fragment: Pas toen Harry de achterdeur uit stampte, de achtertuin in, bedacht hij iets.
findings.problem: Legal and natural (A-SUB-FIRST, 13 words), but the afterthought 'de achtertuin in' after the clause-final verb and before the inverted main clause is a heavier shape than V2's two main clauses; the postposition 'de achterdeur uit' is also a step up from 'door de achterdeur naar buiten'.
findings.evidence: L-SUB satisfied (one subordinate clause); recorded for the V1/V2/V3 comparison, not as a defect.
findings.required_fix: None required. Lighter alternative if wanted: 'Harry stampte de achterdeur uit, de achtertuin in. Pas toen bedacht hij iets.'

findings.problem: Gloss on a word the lexicon marks known (pluk = handful, tuft, A2); the slot could be freed.
findings.required_fix: Optional: remove the gloss if b086 ever needs a second gloss elsewhere; otherwise leave.

findings.fragment: ook als ik me dan stom voel
findings.problem: The particle 'dan' inside the als-clause is a small spoken-Dutch filler; without it the clause is cleaner.
findings.evidence: 'ook als ik me stom voel' is the plain form.
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'ook als ik me stom voel'.

findings.problem: Two B1 stretch lemmas in the scene, inside the budget.
findings.evidence: stretch budget 2 vs 8/1000 allowed; both transparent (achter+deur; hersenen recurs for 'brain' per translator note).

flag_decisions.reason: Attributive 'verbaasd' is a plain adjective: lexicon ADJ A1 and named explicitly in restricted.md ('verbaasd … are fine'); look-alike table 'Hij was verbaasd.'

tool_feedback: R-PARTICIPLE on 'verbaasde' (b084) is a false positive: lemma is a lexicon ADJ entry and restricted.md names 'verbaasd' as allowed; skip amod participles whose lemma is a lexicon ADJ, or push confidence under ignore_confidence (0.3).
'wél' reported unknown: the acute stress accent (wél, dát, zó, één) is not normalised before lookup; strip combining acutes for lookup (keep ê/é in gênant/café, which are lexical).
Vocabulary row 'haarne' is a non-word: spaCy lemma of the diminutive 'haarnetje'; strip -tje/-je before lookup and retry compound decomposition (haar + net) on the stripped form.
'drugsgeld' rated hard C1 (pos VERB) from an nt2lex-only hit; the lexicon hit pre-empts compound decomposition, so a transparent compound of two A1 words is reported as hard.
known share 97.9% LOW and density 20.8/1000 HIGH are both artefacts of the three rows above; after dismissal the scene is 2 stretch lemmas ≈ 8.3/1000 and ≥ 99% known.
Glosses on known lemmas (schor, gefluister, plukken) never appear as a table row, so gloss bloat on known words is invisible from the table; add a 'glossed known lemma' row or warning.
Sense-level gap, not a bug: 'behoorlijk' passes as known A2 (adjective 'proper') while the text uses the degree-adverb sense; the lexicon cannot see this, so it stays a reviewer judgement.
